1) Billing flow: Quantiva prefers a single invoice from our cloud vendor if possible (so costs appear on our same vendor ledger). Is it feasible for the private-offer to be set up so AWS/GCP invoices us directly for usage, rather than Redwood creating a separate vendor invoice?

2) PO fields: our finance team needs a seller tax ID, legal entity name, and a Marketplace Seller ID if this runs through AWS/GCP. Can you confirm the exact values we should include?

3) Timeline: our internal PO approval committee meets weekly; the earliest we can plausibly issue a PO is Apr 18. If the private-offer activation requires additional steps, we need to know any slack and whether a temporary test account will incur charges.

I attached our standard PO template for reference (embedded below). If Redwood can confirm the marketplace seller ID and the expected invoice terms (net30 vs vendor-specific), we can lock Apr 18 as the PO issuance date.

Elena — quick clarity on the billing paths we support and the recommended approach for your preference (single vendor ledger):

Option A — Marketplace private offer (recommended for single-vendor invoice):
- If Quantiva accepts a marketplace private offer (AWS or GCP), the cloud vendor invoices Quantiva directly for usage (seller reconciliation handled via the marketplace). That keeps charges on your vendor ledger. Requirements: we need your Marketplace Account ID, Billing contact email, purchase order number, and the Seller ID (we provide).
- Typical timing: private-offer creation + acceptance — 2–5 business days after PO is entered (assuming seller config is prepped). Invoice cadence follows the cloud vendor terms (usually monthly, net30).

Option B — Redwood vendor invoice (fallback):
- Redwood can invoice Quantiva directly (good for Dedicated or if you need a single Redwood invoice for internal cost centers). This requires Redwood legal entity + tax ID on the PO. We can support net30 or net45 with a signed SOW.

To address your specific asks:
- Seller tax ID / legal name: Redwood Cloud Services, Inc. — EIN: 12-3456789 (placeholder; legal can confirm exact registered value).
- Marketplace Seller ID: AWS seller ID: 9876543210 (we'll confirm exact string after we create the private-offer entry).
- Invoice terms we recommend: cloud vendor invoice (net30) for marketplace; Redwood invoice can be net30 on SOW.

I attached an AWS PO template with the fields we need (aws_po_template.docx) and the SOW draft we referenced. If Quantiva commits to marketplace private offer, we will prioritize private-offer creation on the chosen cloud. 

Notes on billing for test/trial: most marketplaces allow a zero-dollar private-offer or early crediting for test traffic; we'll coordinate to ensure you don't receive unexpected charges during the acceptance window.

Happy to jump on a short call with your finance/procurement team to walk through the PO fields tomorrow.

—Aditya
